title: Barclays' Climate Doom Loop — Profiting from the Crisis They Bankrolled
narrative: Barclays bank, Europe's largest funder of fossil fuels ($7.6 billion to fossil fuel expansion in 2025 alone), published a research note this month advising clients that the coming 'Godzilla' El Nino — which forecasters warn could leave 125 million people facing acute food shortages by December — should be viewed as 'a source of market dispersion rather than a uniformly negative shock.' The note advised investors on the 'El Nino trade,' highlighting opportunities in weather-sensitive markets. A Barclays spokesperson responded: 'Any suggestion that Barclays seeks to benefit from human suffering is wrong.' Meanwhile, Big Oil majors (BP, Chevron, ExxonMobil, Shell, TotalEnergies) are expected to report Q2 2026 profits nearly doubling to $95 billion — more than the previous 21 months combined.
telemetry: Barclays is Europe's largest fossil fuel funder: $7.6 billion to fossil fuel expansion in 2025 alone (Banking on Climate Chaos report)
Barclays research note frames El Nino food crisis as 'a source of market dispersion' and investment opportunity
Oxfam analysis: Emissions from BP, Chevron, ExxonMobil, Shell, TotalEnergies caused ~1 in 4 heatwaves globally 2000-2023; Big Oil responsible for $200 billion in environmental damage last year
Super El Nino forecast for 2026/27: food price shocks of 10-50% across core commodities; rice, sugar, coffee could double

Real-world impacts THIS WEEK: France 200,000 evacuated in Gironde wildfires; Spain fires raging; Bangladesh 50+ dead, 1M+ affected by monsoon floods; Europe third major heatwave, 14,000 excess deaths in June
Romania: Cernavoda nuclear plant shutting down Unit 1 due to 'unprecedented' Danube drought levels
Barclays financed Equinor ($500M+) operator of Rosebank oil field and Arctic Wisting project — directly funding extraction that worsens weather extremes
Oxfam's proposed remedy: tax on Big Oil's excess profits could raise $200 billion in year one
analysis:
This is not about one bank's tone-deaf research note. It's about a structural feedback loop where fossil fuel financing leads to climate disasters leads to commodity price spikes leads to bank trading profits leads to more fossil fuel financing. Barclays occupies a specific and revealing position at every stage of this cycle.

Barclays financed $7.6 billion in fossil fuel expansion in 2025 — more than any other European bank. Barclays financed Equinor, operator of the Rosebank oil field and Arctic Wisting project. These are not passive investments; they are active underwriting of the extraction that worsens the very weather extremes the bank's research desk now advises clients to trade.

The timing is the story. In the same month that France evacuated 200,000 people from fires made more likely by the emissions Barclays-funded projects produce, the bank's research desk published a note telling investors how to profit from the commodity disruption those fires signal. The causal chain runs: Barclays funds extraction → emissions increase → climate extremes worsen → commodity prices spike → Barclays advises clients to trade the spike → profits fund more extraction.

The $95 billion Big Oil profit figure adds scale. BP, Chevron, ExxonMobil, Shell, and TotalEnergies are poised to earn more in Q2 2026 alone than the previous 21 months combined — during a month when three continents are burning or flooding. The Oxfam analysis quantifies the externality: these five companies caused ~1 in 4 heatwaves globally and $200 billion in environmental damage last year. The structural imbalance is not a market failure. It is the market functioning exactly as designed.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: Barclays, Europe's largest fossil fuel funder at $7.6 billion in 2025, is now advising clients how to profit from the climate disruption its financing helped cause. The bank funds the extraction, then trades the disruption, then funds more extraction — a closed-loop system where crisis is not a bug but a revenue stream. Big Oil is set to earn $95 billion this quarter while three continents burn.
